The graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown above. Which of the following is the graph of $y=f(-x)?$
q-16701.worked_solution:
To obtain the graph of $y=f(-x)$ from $y=f(x)$, we need to reflect the graph over the $y$-axis. The resulting graph is shown below.

q-26412.name: Question 3
q-26412.problem: The point $Q$ with coordinates $(1,1)$ lies on the curve $y=f(x).$ Which of the following points must lie on $y=f(-x)?$
q-26412.worked_solution:
The transformation $y=f(-x)$ reflects the curve $y=f(x)$ in the $y$-axis.

First, notice that the point $P(1,1)$ lies $1$ unit to the *right* from the $y$-axis. So, under the action of the transformation, this point will be reflected $1$ unit to the *left* from the $y$-axis.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14253341/assets/e39b804eef0617e89d43808793c844f1223a427493e8b6554cc7ad25477f7ddc.png)

We conclude that the point $(-1,1)$ must lie on the graph of $y=f(-x).$

q-26412.html:
Question 3
?

The point Q with coordinates (1,1) lies on the curve y=f(x). Which of the following points must lie on y=f(−x)?

a
(−1,−1)
b
(−1,1)
c
(1,1)
d
(1,−1)
e
(0,1)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The transformation y=f(−x) reflects the curve y=f(x) in the y-axis.

First, notice that the point P(1,1) lies 1 unit to the right from the y-axis. So, under the action of the transformation, this point will be reflected 1 unit to the left from the y-axis.

We conclude that the point (−1,1) must lie on the graph of y=f(−x).
